messages:
maria: CI publish step failing on master after the Dockerfile refactor, can someone take a quick look?

maria: buildkite job https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4567 -> failed at `docker push` with 403

maria: logs:
```
... pushing layer sha256:abc123
failed to upload layer: server response: 403 Forbidden
error: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
``` 

ci-bot: build 4567 failed · see artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4567/artifacts :eye:

akeem: is this the new slim-stage change from yesterday's PR? @maria which image name/registry did it try to push to?

maria: yes PR #9214 changed the final stage. image: registry.internal.redwood.io/apps/service:pr-9214

jen: 403 on push often means creds expired or token scope missing. Did we rotate the deploy key/token recently?

sam: also worth checking whether the layer digest changed vs what's referenced in the manifest. seen that when multi-stage outputs reorder files.

lucy: quick triage: can you paste the full `docker push` snippet? sometimes it's `blob unknown to registry` vs `denied` which are different causes

maria: full snippet below:
```
Sending build context to Docker daemon  12.34MB
Step 15/18 : COPY --from=builder /app/dist /app/dist
 ---> 3e2f4d7a
Successfully built 7c9f1a2b
Successfully tagged registry.internal.redwood.io/apps/service:pr-9214
The push refers to repository [registry.internal.redwood.io/apps/service]
Pushing [==================================================>]  9.3MB
failed to upload layer: upload failed: unauthorized: authentication required
```

akeem: that's "unauthorized" not "blob unknown". probably auth token problem. Which pipeline credentials are used for push (service principal / CI role)?

maria: pipeline uses `CI_REGISTRY_TOKEN` from vault path secret/ci/registry/prod-token (same token used by other repos)

jen: @akeem can you confirm token rotation schedule? ops team rotated a token last week but should've updated vault.

akeem: checked -- no rotation on that path. However, registry audited a short-lived push token rotation earlier for an emergency. I'm going to check registry logs.

ops-bot: Registry audit link: https://registry.internal.redwood.io/audit/2026-03-08/job-4567 (requires ops access)

sam: in parallel, try a manual `docker login` from a dev VM with that token to rule out CI vault inject step:
```
echo $CI_REGISTRY_TOKEN | docker login --username ci-bot --password-stdin registry.internal.redwood.io
docker push registry.internal.redwood.io/apps/service:pr-9214
```

maria: running manual login now, will report.

(maria posts 2m later)

maria: manual login succeeded but push still 403. registry response shows `policy: deny for mediaType application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip` — maybe new content type flagged by security policy

lucy: ah, we changed the final stage to include a compressed layer (gzip) from the builder. Security team started blocking certain media types for unscanned layers last month.

jen: that fits — change in Dockerfile produces a layer type not allowed by policy. either change Dockerfile to avoid that or add scanning exemption for this workflow.

akeem: short-term: re-run build with `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` or add `--compress=false` to see if archive format changes. also try `docker push --disable-content-trust`? but be careful.

maria: I kicked a rerun with `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 NO_CACHE=1` (pipeline param). re-run id 4568.

ci-bot: build 4568 queued

(maria posts 4m later)

maria: rerun finished — push succeeded! so BuildKit compression was the trigger.

sam: ok great. Next steps: revert the slim-stage change to avoid this compression pattern OR add a pipeline step to run the allowed media-type preservation (and update docs).

jen: I'll open a quick follow-up PR that forces uncompressed final layer or uses `--output type=docker` variant that we've validated. @maria can you attach the failing image tar for security to inspect before we relax policy?

maria: attaching artifact now to the build.security channel and pinging sec-team.

ops-bot: created incident #REG-172: Push blocked by media-type policy. assigned to sec-team.

lucy: cc: @sec-team please review artifact from build 4567 — likely a false positive due to BuildKit default compression.

maria: thanks all, marking this thread resolved for triage. will keep follow-up PR notes in #eng-infra.

jen: thanks — and add a bullet in the release notes about BuildKit behavior and registry policy.

maria: will do :white_check_mark:
